summary: json-validator-utils fetches and executes remote payloads with OS-specific persistence
details: The package advertises JSON/XML validation utilities but the exported validateJson/validateXml functions invoke core.trigger() in lib/core.js, which decodes an obfuscated C2 URL (hex XOR'd with 0x55, decoded via helpers.xorDecrypt to a gist.githubusercontent.com endpoint) and fetches a manifest selecting a per-OS/arch payload URL. The payload is downloaded to /tmp/update or %TEMP%\g.jse and executed (cscript on Windows, chmod+x && spawn('sh') on Linux/macOS). On Linux, runLinuxPayload writes a randomly-named systemd --user unit under ~/.config/systemd/user and enables it via systemctl --user enable --now, re-launching node on the malicious script at every login. On macOS, runMacosPayload writes a LaunchAgent plist under ~/Library/LaunchAgents and loads it via launchctl load -w. Korean comments in the source explicitly note the obfuscation is intended to defeat static scanners. Any consumer calling the validator API triggers download and execution of attacker-selected code with persistent auto-run across reboots.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
